To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

A constrained discrete-time linear dynamical system is vulnerable to an actuation attack if the spectral radius of its dynamics is greater than the ratio of the size of its state constraint set to the size of its input constraint set, and the attack is allowed to inject more than a certain proportion of the total input to the system.
a sufficient condition under actuation attack for a constrained linear system to be controllable is that its spectral radius is less than one.

a system with a large spectral radius, a large state constraint set relative to the input constraint set, and a large portion of the input constraint allowed to the attacker, is more vulnerable to actuation attacks that drive the states of the plant to the boundary of the state constraint set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can the actuation attack be designed to cause the largest deviation of the states from the state constraint set?
the development of a set-theoretical framework for analysing the impact of actuation attacks on constrained discrete-time linear systems.
the following question: how much control authority can an actuation attacker have before the system becomes unstable?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

if the attacker is allowed to inject a fraction of the input larger than a function of the spectral norm of the system, and if the attacker is able to inject the same fraction of the input for all states, then the system is not stabilizable.
if the spectral radius is less than the ratio between the size of the state and input constraint sets, then the system is not vulnerable to actuation attacks.

, if the system is unstable, the attacker can always cause the state constraint set to be violated, regardless of the size of the input constraint sets; and if the system is stable, the attacker can only cause the state constraint to be violated if the input constraint set is sufficiently large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a system subject to actuations attacks, if we know the spectral radius and we can bound the relative sizes of input and state constraint set, and the proportion that is allowed to the attacker, then we can determine if there exists a state constraint set that is invariant under the actuation attacks.
the system is not robust to actuation attacks if the system is unstable and the input constraint set is large relative to the state constraint set.
, in the presence of actuation attacks, the attacker can drive the state of a constrained system out of the constraint set if the system is not sufficiently stable.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a constrained linear system subject to a bounded actuation attack, there exists a finite upper bound on the size of the input constraint sets, which, if exceeded, will result in an unbounded state constraint set for the closed-loop system.
the attacker can only cause the states of the constrained system to escape the state constraints if the attacker is able to control a sufficiently large proportion of the total input to the system.
the spectral radius of a linear system plays an important role in the design of resilient control systems.
